about: English meaning written for this library (en-scriptures) from the Gurmukhi, line by line, with a few notes (tools/meanings/style.md §12); Prof. Sahib Singh's Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka, Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya, the Shabdarth and the published translations were read to check each reading, never copied (tools/meanings/overlap.py).

8.1: So Dar: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
What is that gate of yours like, and what is that home like, where (you) sit and take care of all?
The sounds of your countless instruments of many kinds play there, and so many are the musicians who play for you.
So many of your ragas, with their raginis, are sung there, and so many are your singers.
Wind, water and fire sing of you; Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) sings of you at your door.
Chitr and Gupt, who know how to write, sing of you; what they write, Dharam Raj weighs and judges.
Shiva, Brahma and the goddesses sing of you, ever beautiful, adorned by you.
The Indras, seated on their thrones, sing of you with the gods at your door.
The Siddhas sing of you in samadhi (deep meditative absorption); the sadhus sing of you in contemplation.
The celibates, the charitable and the contented sing of you; the mighty heroes sing of you.
The pandits and the great rishis who read (the scriptures) sing of you, age after age, along with the Vedas.
The enchanting women who charm the mind sing of you, in heaven, in the mortal world and in the netherworld.
The jewels you have created sing of you, along with the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
Warriors of great might and heroes sing of you; the four sources of life sing of you.
The regions, the worlds and the universes, made and set in place by you, sing of you.
They alone sing of you who please you, your devotees, steeped (in your love) and full of delight.
So many others sing of you who do not come to my mind; what can Nanak consider?
He, he alone, is ever true; the Master is true, and true is his glory.
He is, and he will be; he does not depart, nor will he depart, he who made the creation.
He who brought forth Maya of many colours, many kinds and many species
watches over what he has made, having made it, as befits his greatness.
Whatever pleases him, that he will do; no command can then be given (to him).
He is the King, the Emperor over kings; O Nanak, (our part is) to live in his will.
9.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Everyone calls you great, (O God,) having heard (it from others),
but how great you are is (told) only on seeing you.
Your worth cannot be fixed, nor can you be put into words.
Those who speak of you stay merged in you.
O my great Master, deep and profound, fathomless in virtues,
no one knows how much, how vast, your expanse is.
All who practise surat (attention fixed on God) joined together and practised it;
all who weigh worth joined together and weighed (yours);
yet by the men of knowledge, the men of meditation, the teachers and the teachers of teachers,
not even a sesame seed's worth of your greatness could be told.
All truthfulness, all austerities, all good deeds,
and the great powers of the Siddhas, the accomplished ones:
without you, no one has attained this siddhi (accomplishment).
It comes by (your) grace, and then no one can hold it back.
What can the poor speaker (say)?
Your storehouses are filled with praises.
The one to whom you give (your praise), what can anyone do against him?
O Nanak, the True One (himself) is the one who adorns (him).
9.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When I utter (his Name), I live; when it is forgotten, I die.
The True Name is hard to utter.
If hunger for the True Name arises,
then, eating (of the Name) in that hunger, the sorrows are driven away.
Why should he be forgotten, O my mother?
The Master is true, and (is found) through the True Name.
Of the True Name's greatness, even a sesame seed's worth,
they have grown weary telling, yet none has found its worth.
If all were to join together and set about describing him,
he does not become greater, nor does he become less.
He does not die, nor is there mourning (for him).
He keeps on giving, and what he gives to be enjoyed never runs out.
This is his quality: there is no other (like him);
none has been, and none will be.
As great as you yourself are, so great is your gift,
(you,) who made the day and made the night.
Those who forget the Master are low-born;
O Nanak, those without the Name are the outcastes.
10.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O servant of the Lord, True Guru, True Being, I make my plea before you, Guru:
we are lowly worms and insects, True Guru, come to your refuge; be merciful, and make the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) shine (in us).
O my friend, divine Guru, make the Lord's Name shine in me.
May the Naam, received through the Guru's teaching, be the companion of my life, and the Lord's praise my provision for the road.
Great, very great, is the fortune of the Lord's servants who have faith in the Lord, Har Har, and a thirst for the Lord.
On receiving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; and in the Sangat (the company of the holy), virtues shine forth in them.
Those who have not found the Lord's sweet essence, the Naam, are unfortunate, and in the grip of Jam (the messenger of Death).
Those who have not come to the True Guru's refuge and his Sangat: cursed is their living, and cursed their hope of life.
The servants of the Lord who have found the True Guru's Sangat had this written on their foreheads by the Lord from the start.
Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), in which the Lord's sweet essence is found; O Nanak, in meeting the Lord's servants, the Naam shines forth within.
10.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, why do you keep brooding over your efforts (to earn), when the dear Lord is engaged in the task (of caring for you)?
He has created creatures in rocks and stones, and set their food ready for them beforehand.
O my dear Lord (Madho), whoever has joined the Sat Sangat has crossed over.
By the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state; the dry wood has turned green.
Mother, father, people, sons, wife: no one is anyone's support.
The Master delivers sustenance to each and every one; O mind, why are you afraid?
(The crane) comes flying hundreds of kos (leagues), her little ones left behind.
Who is there to feed them, to give them grain to peck? She keeps them remembered in her mind.
All the treasures and the eighteen siddhis rest in the palm of the Master's hand.
O servant Nanak, let us be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to him; (O Lord,) your extent has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
10.3: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji): So Purakh.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.

That Purakh, the Being who pervades all, is Niranjan, free of the stain of Maya (the world's illusion and lure); the Lord, the all-pervading Being, is free of that stain; the Lord is beyond reach, wholly beyond reach, without limit.
O Lord, the eternal Creator, all meditate on you, all meditate on you.
All beings are yours, Lord; you are the Giver to every being.
Meditate on the Lord, revered Sants (saints): he makes all sorrows pass away.
The Lord himself is the Master, and the Lord himself the servant; O Nanak, what is a poor creature (by itself)?
You are within every heart, and in all without any gap; O Lord, you, the one Being, pervade all.
Some are givers and some are beggars; all these are your wondrous plays.
You are the giver yourself, and yourself the one who enjoys (the gifts); apart from you I know no other.
You are the Supreme Lord (Paarbrahm), endless, endless; which of your virtues shall I name and describe?
Those who serve you, those who serve you, Lord: your servant Nanak is a sacrifice to them.
O Lord, those who meditate on you, who meditate on you, live at peace in the world.
Liberated, liberated are those who have meditated on the Lord; the noose of Jam has snapped for them.
Those who have meditated on the Fearless, on the Fearless Lord: he takes away all their fear.
Those who have served, who have served my Lord, merge into the very form of the Lord, Har Har.
Blessed, blessed are those who have meditated on the Lord; your servant Nanak gives himself in sacrifice to them.
The storehouses of devotion to you, of devotion to you, Lord, are full beyond end, beyond all end.
Your devotees, your devotees praise you, O Lord, many, countless, without end.
Many, so many, worship you, O Lord; numberless (beings) practise austerities and repeat (your Name).
Many, so many of yours read the many Simritis and Shastras, and carry out the rites and the six duties.
O servant Nanak, those devotees, those devotees alone are good who are pleasing to my Lord God.
You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator, Lord; no other is as great as you.
In every age you are the One; always, always you are the One; you are the unmoving Creator, ever the same.
O Lord, whatever pleases you yourself, that alone comes about; whatever you yourself do, that takes place.
You yourself brought forth the whole creation, and you yourself, having made it, have destroyed it all.
Servant Nanak sings the virtues of the Creator, who knows each and every one.
11.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
You are the Creator, the abode of truth, my Master.
Whatever pleases you, that alone will be; whatever you give, that alone I receive.
All (creation) is yours; all have meditated on you.
The one to whom you show grace has found the jewel of the Naam.
The Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) found it; the manmukh (the self-willed) lost it.
You yourself have parted (beings from you), and you yourself have united (them).
You are the river; all is within you alone.
Apart from you there is no other.
All beings and creatures are your play.
By the will that parts, even one who had met is separated; by the will that unites, there is meeting (again).
Only the one whom you make to understand comes to know (you),
and he ever speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues.
Whoever has served the Lord has found peace;
in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) he has merged in the Name of the Lord.
You yourself are the Creator; all that happens is your doing.
Apart from you there is no other, no second.
You create and create, watch over (your creation), and know all about it.
O servant Nanak, (the Lord) is revealed within the Gurmukh.
12.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Our) dwelling has come to be in that terrible lake whose water he himself has made fire.
In the mire of attachment the foot cannot move; before our eyes (many) have drowned there.
O mind, O foolish mind, you do not remember the One.
As you forget the Lord, your virtues have wasted away.
I am neither celibate (jati) nor virtuous (sati), nor am I learned; my life has turned out the life of a foolish, ignorant one.
Nanak humbly prays: (let me be) in the refuge of those who have not forgotten you.
12.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You have received this lovely human body;
this is your turn to meet Gobind (the Lord of the universe).
All other tasks are of no use to you at all;
join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and remember the Naam alone.
Set yourself to the task of crossing the ocean of the world;
your life is passing in vain in the love of Maya.
(O Lord,) I have practised neither repetition (of the Name), austerity, self-restraint nor any deed of dharma;
I have not served the Saadh (the holy one), nor have I known you, O Lord, my King.
Says Nanak, we are of lowly deeds;
save the honour of one who has come into your refuge.
12.3: Sohila: Raag Gauri Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon,
in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator.
Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord.
I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever.
Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one).
(O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver?
The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite).
Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master.
To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day.
Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too).
12.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Six are the schools, six (their) teachers, and six (their) teachings;
but the Guru of these teachers is the One (God), whose guises are many.
O brother, the house (the school) in which the Creator is praised:
hold fast to that house; in it lies your greatness.
Visas, chasas, gharis, pahars, lunar days and weekdays (together) make up the month;
the sun is one and the seasons many; (in the same way,) O Nanak, the Creator has so many guises.
13.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The sky is the platter; the sun and the moon are its lamps, and the clusters of stars are like pearls;
the sandal-scented breeze from the Malaya hills is the incense, the wind waves the fly-whisk, and all the plant life blossoms for the Light (that is God).
What a wondrous aarti this is! O Destroyer of the round of births, this is your aarti:
the unstruck sound resounds as its drums.
Thousands are your eyes, yet you have no eye; thousands are your forms, yet not one form is yours;
thousands are your spotless feet, yet you have not one foot; you are without a nose, yet thousands are your noses: these wonders of yours have enchanted me.
Within all is the light, and that light is he.
By his radiance there is light within all.
Through the Guru's teaching this light becomes manifest.
Whatever pleases him, that becomes the aarti.
My mind is lured by the nectar of the Lord's lotus feet; night and day I thirst for it.
Give Nanak, the rain-bird, the water of your grace, by which he may abide in your Name.
13.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The city (of the body) is filled to the brim with lust and anger; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), these are smashed to pieces.
By the writ of the past the Guru has been found, and loving absorption (liv) in the Lord is set like a jewel in the mind.
Join your palms before the Saadh: this is a great merit.
Lie stretched out before him in prostration: this is a great merit.
The Saakats (those who have turned from God) have not known the taste of the Lord's sweet essence; within them is the thorn of Haumai (ego).
The further they walk, the more it pricks and they suffer pain, and they bear the rod of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads.
The Lord's servants remain merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har; they have cut away the pain of birth and death in the world.
They have found the imperishable, all-pervading Supreme God, and great is their glory across the lands and universes.
We are poor and meek, God, and we are yours; save us, O Lord, save us: you are the greatest of the great.
Servant Nanak's support and prop is the Naam; in the Lord's Name alone has peace been found.
13.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I make one request, my friends; listen: this is the time to serve the Sants.
Earn the Lord's profit here before you depart, and your dwelling hereafter will be at ease.
Day and night, the span of life wears away.
O mind, meet the Guru and set your affairs right.
This world is steeped in vice and caught in doubt; the Brahm Giani (one who knows God) has crossed over it.
Whom (God) awakens and gives this sweet essence to drink, that one has come to know the story of the Indescribable.
Buy the very thing you came for; through the Guru, the Lord comes to dwell within the mind.
In your own home within, in the peace of Sahaj, you will find (his) mansion, and there will be no more round (of birth and death).
O Knower of hearts, all-pervading Being, Creator, fulfil the longing of my mind.
Servant Nanak begs for this one joy: make me the dust of the Sants' feet.
14.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If palaces of pearls were to rise (for me), and if they were inlaid with jewels,
plastered with musk, saffron, aloeswood and sandalwood, and delight were to fill (my mind),
I fear that at the sight of it I would lose my way, you would slip from my memory, and your Name would not come to my mind.
Without the Lord, the soul burns to ashes.
I have asked my Guru and seen for myself: there is no other place (but the Lord).
If the floor were set with diamonds and rubies, and the bed studded with rubies,
and an enchanting woman, a jewel shining on her face, were to show her charms with love,
I fear that at the sight of it I would lose my way, you would slip from my memory, and your Name would not come to my mind.
If I became a Siddha (a yogi of perfect powers), worked the siddhis (miraculous powers), and called the riddhis (powers of plenty) to come (and they came),
if I could sit hidden or in plain sight at will, and the world held me in reverence,
I fear that at the sight of it I would lose my way, you would slip from my memory, and your Name would not come to my mind.
If I gathered armies and became a sultan, and set my foot upon the throne,
and, seated there, gave commands and took in revenue, O Nanak, it would all be (empty as) the wind.
I fear that at the sight of it I would lose my way, you would slip from my memory, and your Name would not come to my mind.
14.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If my life lasted millions upon millions (of years), and air alone were my drink and my food,
if, (sitting) in a cave, I saw neither the moon nor the sun, and had no place to sleep even in a dream,
even then your worth could not be reckoned; how great can I say your Name is?
The True One, the Formless Lord, abides in his own being.
Hearing and hearing (from others), we speak of him; if it pleases him, he brings forth the longing (to praise him).
If I were slain, cut to pieces again and again, put in the mill and ground,
burnt in the fire, and mingled with the ashes,
even then your worth could not be reckoned; how great can I say your Name is?
If I became a bird and roamed the air, and went up to hundreds of skies,
no one could see me, and I neither drank nor ate anything,
even then your worth could not be reckoned; how great can I say your Name is?
O Nanak, if there were paper by the hundred thousand maunds, and, reading and reading (what is written on it), love (for you) were felt,
if the ink never ran short, and I drove the pen like the wind,
even then your worth could not be reckoned; how great can I say your Name is?
15.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
By measured count we speak; by measured count we eat;
by measured count we walk the road (of life); by measured count we hear and see;
by measured count are the breaths we are made to draw: why should I go and ask a learned man (about it)?
O brother, the play of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) is a deception.
The blind one has forgotten the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered); he is left with neither this (Maya) nor that (the Naam).
From birth until death, life here is devoured by death.
Where one is seated and made to understand (the account of one's deeds), there no one has gone along.
All those who weep (for the dead) are only tying up bundles of straw.
Everyone says, more and more (wealth); no one says less;
no one has found its true worth, and by mere saying no one becomes great.
You alone are the True Master, (O Lord); the many other beings and worlds (pass away).
Those who are of the lowest caste among the low, lower still than the lowest:
Nanak is with them, their companion; what has he to do with vying with the great?
Where the lowly are cared for, there is your gracious glance, your blessing.
15.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Greed is a dog (within me), falsehood the sweeper, and what I eat by cheating is carrion;
slander of others is nothing but others' filth in my mouth, and the fire of anger is the chandal (outcaste);
relishes and cravings, and praising myself: these are my deeds, O my Creator.
O brother, let us speak (such words) as bring honour.
They alone are the best who are called the best at (the Lord's) door; one of low deeds sits and weeps.
The relish of gold, the relish of silver, of women, the relish of the scent of perfumes,
the relish of horses, the relish of beds and palaces, the relish of sweets, the relish of meat:
when the body has so many relishes, in which heart can the Naam find a dwelling?
The word by whose speaking honour is gained, that word spoken is accepted.
By speaking insipid words one comes to ruin; listen, foolish and ignorant mind.
Those who please him are good; what (use) is there in any other talk and telling?
Theirs is wisdom, theirs is honour, and theirs the wealth in their lap, in whose hearts (the Lord) stays absorbed.
What praise can be given them? Who else is so beautiful?
O Nanak, those outside (the Lord's) gracious glance stay absorbed in (his) gifts, not in the Name.
15.3: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Giver has handed out the opium pill of falsehood;
drunk on it, (people) have forgotten death and made merry for four days.
The True One has met those sober ones (who keep clear of this drug), who (strive) to hold fast to his court.
O Nanak, know the True One to be true,
serving whom peace is found, and one stays in honour in your court, (O Lord).
Truth is the wine made without molasses, the wine in which is the True Name.
All who hear (of it) and speak (of it): I am a sacrifice to them.
Only when the mind finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion is it truly known to be drunk.
(When) the Name and good deeds are the water (to bathe in), and truthful living the perfume that scents the body,
then the face shines bright; of a hundred thousand gifts, this is the one gift.
Sorrows are to be told to him alone with whom all comforts are.
Why put out of mind the one to whom the soul and the breath of life belong?
Without him, all that is worn and all that is eaten is impure.
All other talk is false; what pleases you is accepted.
16.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Burn attachment, grind it into ink, and make your intellect the finest paper;
make love the pen and your mind the writer; and, asking the Guru, write the reflection (he gives);
write the Naam, write (his) praise, write that he has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
O brother, learn to write this account,
so that, where the account is called for, it may stand as the true seal (of passage).
Where glories are bestowed, and there is joy forever and delight forever,
(there) the marks of honour appear on the brows of those whose minds hold the True Name.
Only if (the Lord's) grace is there is (the Name) received; not by idle, empty talk.
Some come, and some rise and depart; (some) are given the names of chiefs.
Some are made to be beggars, while some hold great courts.
On going ahead (to the world beyond) it is known that without the Name (all) is worthless.
In fear of you, (O Lord,) my dread is great; worn out with striving, the body wastes away.
Those whose names were sultans and khans have been seen turning to dust.
O Nanak, when one rises and departs, all false loves are broken.
16.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To accept (the Name) is (to me) all the sweet flavours, and to hear it, the salty ones;
to utter (it) with the mouth, the sour and tangy, and to raise (its) sound (in Kirtan), the spices;
love of the One is the thirty-six ambrosial dishes, (given to the one) on whom (the Lord) casts his gracious glance.
O brother, the pleasure of any other food brings ruin,
by eating which the body is pained and vices stir in the mind.
A mind dyed (in his love) is (my) red attire; truthfulness and charity are my white;
cutting away the blackness (of the mind) is my blue; and meditation on (your) feet, my robe;
contentment is (my) waistband; your Name is (my) wealth and my youth.
O brother, the pleasure of any other dress brings ruin,
by wearing which the body is pained and vices stir in the mind.
To understand your way, (O Lord,) is (my) horses, with saddles and golden trappings;
striving for virtues is (my) quiver, arrows, bow, spear and sword-belt;
to stand out with honour is (my) drum and lance; your grace is my caste.
O brother, the pleasure of any other riding brings ruin,
by riding which the body is pained and vices stir in the mind.
The joy of the Name is (my) house and palace; your gracious glance is my family.
What pleases you is (my) command; anything more that could be said is vast and endless.
O Nanak, the True King does not ask anyone in deciding.
O brother, the pleasure of any other sleep brings ruin,
by sleeping in which the body is pained and vices stir in the mind.
17.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One whose body is (pure as) saffron, whose tongue is (set with) the jewels (of praise), and every breath in whose body has the fragrance of aloeswood,
on whose brow is the mark of the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: in that heart the intellect blossoms;
with that intellect alone the True Name, the treasure of virtues, is praised.
O brother, any other wisdom (leads) elsewhere, ever elsewhere.
Though it be practised a hundred times, through falsehood only falsehood gains strength.
(If one) comes to be worshipped, is called a pir (a spiritual guide), and the whole world comes to meet him,
if he spreads his own name and is counted among the Siddhas,
yet if his honour does not count in (the Lord's) reckoning, all that worship is only disgrace.
Those whom the True Guru has established, no one can erase.
Within them is the treasure of the Naam, and the Naam alone shines forth (from them).
The Name is worshipped, the Name is held in faith; he is unbroken, forever true.
When dust is mingled with dust, what becomes of the soul?
All clever schemes are burnt away, and one rises and departs weeping.
O Nanak, if the Name is forgotten, what will become of one on reaching (the Lord's) door?
17.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The virtuous (soul-bride) tells at length of (the Lord's) virtues; the one without virtue pines in regret.
O bride, if you long for your Husband, the Beloved is not met through falsehood.
There is no boat and no raft; the Beloved is far away, and (so) he is not reached.
My Master sits unshaken on his perfect throne.
If he makes one perfect through the Guru, the True and Immeasurable One is found.
God is a beautiful Harimandir (the temple of the Lord), and in it are rubies and gems,
pearls and spotless diamonds, (and around it) a lovely fortress of gold.
Without a ladder, how can I climb the fortress? By meditating on the Lord through the Guru, he is beheld.
The Guru is the ladder, the Guru the boat; the Guru is the raft of the Lord's Name.
The Guru is the pool, the ocean and the ship; the Guru is the place of pilgrimage and the river.
If it pleases him, I am made bright and pure, and go to bathe in the pool of truth.
He is called perfect, perfect; his dwelling is on the perfect throne.
In his perfect and beautiful place, he fulfils the hopes of the hopeless.
O Nanak, if one meets the Perfect One, how can one's virtues fall short?
17.3: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Come, sisters, dear companions, let us hold one another close in embrace;
and, meeting, let us tell the stories of our all-powerful Husband.
All virtues are the True Master's; all faults are ours.
O Creator, everyone is in your power.
Let us reflect on the one Shabad (the Word): when you are (with us), what is there besides?
Go and ask the happy wives: by what virtues have you enjoyed (your Husband's) love?
(They say:) We are adorned with Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), with contentment and with sweet speech;
the Beloved, the source of delight, is met when the Guru's Shabad is heard.
How many are your powers, how great your gifts!
How many beings and creatures are yours, praising you day and night!
How many are your forms and colours, how many (beings) of caste and without caste!
When the True One is met, truth wells up, and through truth one merges into the True One.
Awareness awakens, honour rises, and through the Guru's words one holds (God) in awe.
O Nanak, the True King himself unites (such a one with himself).
18.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
It has gone well: (my soul) has been saved, and Haumai (ego) has died out of the house of my heart.
The enemies, (the vices,) have turned round and taken to serving (me): I have the True Guru's assurance.
I have given up vain fretful imaginings; the True One, free of all care, (now dwells within).
O mind, when the True One is found, fear goes away.
Without the fear (of God), how is anyone to become free of fear? Through the Guru one merges in the Shabad.
However much is said, the saying never comes to an end.
So many are those who beg; the Giver is that One alone.
He whose are the soul and the breath of life: when he dwells in the mind, there is peace.
The world is a dream, a show that has been staged; in an instant (the Lord) has the play played out.
By the will that unites, (beings) meet and come together; by the will that parts, (each) rises and departs.
What pleases him, that alone happens; no other thing can be done.
Through the Guru the real commodity (of the Name) is bought: the true merchandise, the true capital.
Those who have traded in the truth win the perfect Guru's approval.
O Nanak, the one who holds the true merchandise will recognise the worth of the commodity.
18.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As metal melts back into metal, so the one who praises merges, through praise, in the Lord who is worthy of praise.
On him rises the true, fast colour, a deep red like the red poppy (gulal).
The True One is found by the contented, who repeat the Lord's Name in love of the One alone.
O brother, (become) the dust of the feet of the Sants (saints).
In the assembly of the Sants the Guru is found, the wish-fulfilling cow (Kamdhenu) that gives the treasure of liberation.
High and beautiful is (the Lord's) place; above (all) stands the mansion of Murari (the Lord).
By offering true conduct, and through love, his gate, his home, his mansion are reached.
Through the Guru the mind is taught to understand, by reflecting on the Lord who pervades every soul (Atam Ram).
When deeds of the three kinds, (under Maya's three qualities,) are done, hope and anxiety follow.
How shall the knitted brow of inner fretting be loosened without the Guru? Peace comes when one meets (the Lord) in Sahaj.
In one's own home within, (the Lord's) mansion is recognised, when he casts his glance of grace and washes away the filth.
Without the Guru the filth does not come off; without the Lord, how can one dwell in one's (true) home?
Let the one Shabad alone be reflected upon; (whoever does so) gives up every other hope.
To the one who has seen (the Lord) and shows him (to others), Nanak is ever a sacrifice.
18.3: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Cursed is the life of the forsaken soul-bride, robbed through the love of another.
Like a wall of kallar (salt-eaten earth), day and night she crumbles and falls down.
Without the Shabad there is no peace; without the Husband (Lord) the pain does not go.
O young bride, what use is adornment without the Husband?
She finds no shelter at his gate or in his home; in the Lord's court the false is put to shame.
He himself is wise and does not err: the True One is the great farmer.
First he prepares the soil (of the heart), then sows the seed of the True Name.
There springs up the one Name, the nine treasures; by (his) grace the mark (of approval) is set.
One who knowingly fails to know the Guru: what good ways, what conduct has he?
The blind one has forgotten the Naam; for the manmukh (the self-willed) there is pitch darkness.
His coming and going does not end; he dies and is born again, and is ruined.
(A bride) had sandalwood bought and brought, saffron, and vermilion for the parting of her hair;
scented oil (choa) and sandal in great plenty, and camphor with the betel leaves;
but if the bride does not please her Husband, then all this show is false.
All enjoyment of pleasures is in vain; all adornments are worthless.
So long as one is not pierced by the Shabad, how can one look beautiful at the Guru's door?
O Nanak, blessed are the happy soul-brides who love their Husband Lord.
19.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body, left empty, is fearful to see when the soul goes out from within it.
The fire (of life) that was burning has gone out; no smoke (of breath) rises at all.
The five (senses) weep, full of grief, having wasted away in the love of another.
O fool, repeat the Name of Ram, the Lord, keeping his virtues in your heart.
Through Haumai, through the enticing sense of mine, through pride, the whole (world) is being robbed.
Those who have forgotten the Naam, taken up with other pursuits,
clinging to double-mindedness, have burned away and died, with the fire of craving within.
Those whom the Guru protected were saved; the rest were robbed by the cheat of worldly affairs.
Affection has died, love has gone; enmity and strife have died.
The running after affairs is spent; ego has died, and the sense of mine, Maya and anger.
By grace (the Guru) is met, and the True One is found; through the Guru the mind is ever held back (from vice).
Through true work the True One is met, when the Guru's teaching is taken to heart.
That person is not born and does not die; he neither comes nor goes.
O Nanak, he is held in honour at (the Lord's) gate; he goes to the Lord's court robed in honour.
19.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body, burning and burning, has turned to dust; the mind, in the love of Maya, has become iron slag (manoor).
Even so the faults stay on as its enemies; it blows its trumpet in falsehood.
Without the Shabad one is made to wander; double-mindedness drowns the whole boatload.
O mind, cross over through the Shabad, fixing your attention on it.
One who has not understood the Naam through the Guru dies and is born, and keeps coming and going.
That body alone is called pure in which the True Name dwells;
the body steeped in the fear (of God) and in the True One, whose tongue savours the True One.
One whom (the Lord) looks upon with his true glance of grace is not put again into the heat (of the crucible of births).
From the True One came air, and from air came water;
from water he fashioned the three worlds, and set his light in every heart.
The Immaculate One does not become soiled (though in every heart); those steeped in the Shabad receive honour.
The one whose mind has found contentment in the True One, on him (the Lord) casts his glance of grace.
His (body of) five elements is steeped in the True One and in his fear; the true light (shines) in his mind.
O Nanak, his faults are left behind; the Guru has kept his honour.
20.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, it is in the boat of truth that the crossing is made, through reflection on the Guru's teaching.
Some come and some go, whole boatloads, full of pride.
By the stubborn mind's own counsel one drowns; the Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) is carried across by the True One.
Without the Guru, how can one cross over and find peace?
As it pleases you, (O Lord,) so keep (me); I have no other, no second.
Ahead I see the forest fire burning; behind, green shoots are sprouting.
From whom (the world) springs, by him it perishes; the True One fills every heart.
You yourself, (O Lord,) bring (beings) into union with you, into your presence in the true mansion.
With every breath may I remember you, and never forget you.
The more the Master dwells in my mind, the more may I, through the Guru, drink the Amrit (the nectar of the Name).
Mind and body are yours, and you are (my) Master; may I cast off pride and merge (in you).
He who brought forth this world and gave the three worlds their visible form,
that Light is known through the Guru; for the foolish manmukh there is only darkness.
(His) light is in every heart, without a gap; through the Guru's teaching one understands this essence.
Those who have known (him) through the Guru are acclaimed.
They blend and become one with the True One; the virtues of the True One shine forth (in them).
O Nanak, they are content in the Naam; their soul and body are in God's keeping.
20.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Listen, O mind, my dear friend: meet (the Lord); this is the time.
While youth and breath remain, only so long is this body of use as a body.
Without virtue it is of no use; the body will fall and become a mound of dust.
O my mind, earn the profit (here) and go home.
Through the Guru let the Naam be praised; then the fire of Haumai is put out.
Hearing and hearing, people piece (learning) together; writing and reading, they study loads (of books);
(yet within,) day and night, craving runs high, with the disease of Haumai and vice.
He is free of all care, beyond all weighing; through the Guru's teaching, come to know his worth.
If I were to practise a hundred thousand clevernesses, and keep love and friendship with a hundred thousand,
without the company of the Saadh (the holy one) there is no fulfilment; without the Name there is sorrow and torment.
O my soul, by repeating the Lord's Name one is set free; the Gurmukh comes to know his own self.
To the Guru I have sold my body and mind; I have given him my mind, and my head along with it.
(The One) I searched for, scouring the three worlds, I have beheld (within), searching through the Guru.
The True Guru has brought (me) into union; O Nanak, that God is right with (me).
20.3: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is no anxiety about dying, and no longing for living.
You, (O Lord,) sustain all beings; their every breath and every morsel is in your account.
You dwell within the Gurmukh; as it pleases you, so you decide.
O my soul, repeating the Name of Ram, win the mind over (to it).
The burning that had caught within is quenched; through the Guru the knowledge (of God) has been found.
The state within comes to be known when one meets the Guru, casting off all doubt.
The home to which one goes after dying: (reach) it while still alive, dying (to self) and slaying (the ego).
Through the beautiful unstruck (Anhad) Shabad, by reflecting on the Guru's teaching, (that home) is reached.
When the unstruck Bani is attained, there Haumai is destroyed.
Whoever serves his True Guru, to him I am ever a sacrifice.
He is led to the Lord's court and robed in honour, in whose mouth the Lord's Name dwells.
Wherever I look, (beings) are caught up in the union of Shiv and Shakti.
The body is bound by the three qualities (of Maya); whoever has come into the world (plays) this game.
Those parted (from the Lord) live in the sorrow of separation; the manmukhs find no union.
The mind detached (from Maya) dwells in its own home, when it is dyed in the fear of the True One.
It enjoys the supreme delight of divine knowledge, and hunger (for Maya) does not come again.
O Nanak, subdue this mind and meet (the Lord); then sorrow will not come again.
21.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
This mind is foolish and greedy; attached to greed, it stays caught in greed.
The Saakat (the worshipper of Maya) is not softened by the Shabad; through his evil mind his coming and going goes on.
If the holy True Guru is met, then the treasure of virtues (the Lord) is found.
O mind, give up Haumai and pride.
Serve the Guru, who is the Lord, the sacred pool, and you will be honoured in the Lord's court.
Repeat the Name of Ram day and night; through the Guru, come to know the wealth of the Lord.
All comforts and the delights of the Lord are enjoyed, and divine knowledge (is gained), by joining the assembly of the Sants.
Ever, day and night, the Lord God is served by the one to whom the True Guru has given the Naam.
(The self-willed one) practises falsehood like a dog; slandering the Guru, he burns and is consumed.
Led astray by doubt, he suffers great pain; Jam (the messenger of Death) beats him and threshes him (like grain on the threshing floor).
As a manmukh, no peace is found; as a Gurmukh, there is wondrous peace.
Here (in the world) one is worn down by worldly affairs; (there) only the record of truth is accepted.
The Guru serves the Lord, the true Friend; the Guru's way of living stands supreme (in the Lord's court).
O Nanak, the Naam is not forgotten by one on whom, by the True One's grace, the mark (of approval) is set.
21.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the Beloved is forgotten even for a sesame seed's worth of time, a great disease (seizes) the mind.
How can honour be found in the Lord's court, when the Lord does not dwell in the mind?
Meeting the Guru, peace is found; (absorbed) in (God's) virtues, the fire (of craving) dies out.
O mind, cherish the Lord's virtues day and night.
Those who do not forget the Naam for an instant, for a moment: such people are rare in the world.
When one's light is merged in the Light, and one's awareness joined with the Lord of all awareness,
cruelty and Haumai are wholly gone, and no dread or grief remains.
The one in whose mind the Lord dwells through the Guru, the Guru brings to the meeting (with the Lord).
If I make my body a bride, the Enjoyer (the Husband Lord) takes delight in her.
Do not set your love on what is plainly passing away.
Through the Guru the happy soul-brides enjoy his union; that God is the Husband of their (heart's) bed.
Put out the four fires and die (to self), pouring on them, through the Guru, the water of the Lord's Name.
Within, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, filled to the brim with Amrit.
O Nanak, make the True Guru your friend, and you will go to the Lord's court and find the True One.
22.1: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O beloved, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; taking the Guru's teaching, speak (the Name of) the Lord.
When the mind is put to the touchstone of Truth, it is found to be of full weight.
(Then) no one can set a price on the ruby of the heart; it is beyond all price.
O brother, the diamond that is the Lord is within the Guru.
In the Sat Sangat (the company of the true) the True Guru is found; (there,) through the Shabad, praise (God) day and night.
Gather the true merchandise, the wealth and the capital; it is found by the light the Guru gives.
As fire dies when water is poured on it, so craving dies in one who becomes the servant of (God's) servants.
Cruel Jam cannot touch (such a one); in this way he crosses the terrifying world-ocean, all the way across.
Falsehood does not please the Gurmukhs; they are steeped in the True One, in the love of the True.
Truth does not please the Saakat; the standing of the false is false.
Those whom the Guru unites are steeped in the True One; the true merge in the True One.
Within the mind is the Naam: the ruby, the red gem, the jewel, the precious thing, the diamond.
The Naam is the true merchandise and wealth; the deep, unfathomable (Lord) is in every heart.
O Nanak, (this Naam) is found through the Guru when the Lord, the Diamond, shows mercy.
22.2: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Wandering does not quench the fire (of craving), even if one roams from land to foreign land.
The filth within is not washed away; cursed is such a life, cursed such a garb.
Nowhere else can devotion come about without the True Guru's teaching.
O mind, through the Guru, put out the fire (of craving).
When the Guru's word dwells in the mind, Haumai and craving are put to death.
The mind is a priceless ruby; in the Lord's Name it wins honour.
Joining the Sat Sangat and, through the Guru, fixing loving attention on the Lord, one finds the Lord.
Self-conceit has gone and peace has been found, as water, meeting water, merges into it.
One who has not remembered the Name of the Lord, Har Har, comes and goes (in birth and death), caught in his faults.
One who has not met the True Guru, the great Being, is consumed again and again in the terrifying world-ocean.
This soul is a priceless ruby, (yet) in this way it goes in exchange for a cowrie shell.
Those whom the True Guru meets in love are complete and wise.
Meeting the Guru, one crosses the terrifying world-ocean and is accepted with honour in the Lord's court.
O Nanak, radiant are the faces of those in whom the melody wells up and the Shabad beats like a drum.
22.3: Sri Raag, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Trade, O traders, and take good care of your merchandise.
Buy such goods as will stay with you to the end.
Ahead is the wise Banker; he will examine the goods with care before he takes them.
O brother, utter the Lord's Name with your mind fixed on him.
Take the Lord's praise with you as your merchandise; the Master will see it and be satisfied.
How can there be peace for those who do not have the capital of Truth?
Trading in what is false makes mind and body false.
Like a deer caught in a snare, he suffers greatly and weeps every day.
Counterfeit (coins) are not put into the treasury; such ones do not have the sight of the Lord and the Guru.
The counterfeit have neither standing nor honour; by falseness no one succeeds.
The false one practises only falseness; he came (into the world) and went away, his honour lost.
O Nanak, let the mind be taught through the Guru's Shabad of praise.
Those steeped in the love of the Lord's Name carry no burden (of sin), and do not wander in doubt.
Repeating the Lord's Name brings great profit, and the Fearless Lord (comes to dwell) in the mind.
23.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Wealth, youth and the little flower are guests for only four days.
Like the leaves of the paban (the four-leaved water clover), they wither, droop and pass away.
Enjoy the delight (of the Lord's love), dear one, while youth is fresh and in full swing.
The days are few; when they are spent, the robe (of the body) has grown old.
My dear, joyful friends have gone and fallen asleep in the graveyard.
I too, torn in two minds, must go; I weep in a faint voice.
O fair bride, why do you not hear the news with your own ears,
that you must surely go to your in-laws' home, and your parents' home is not for ever?
O Nanak, she who sleeps (heedless) in her parents' home, know that her house is broken into in broad daylight.
She has lost her little bundle of virtues, and sets off with her faults tied up.
23.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He himself is the one full of relish, he himself the relish, and he himself the one who enjoys it.
He himself becomes the bride in her gown; he himself is the bed and the Husband.
My Master is steeped in love; he pervades all, filling everything.
Fisherman and fish are he himself; he himself is water and net.
The net's weighting bead is he himself, and he himself the red bait within it.
My Beloved, O friend, is himself playful in many ways.
He ever delights in the fortunate wives; look at my state!
Nanak humbly prays: you are the lake, you are the swan.
You are the lotus, you are the water-lily; you yourself behold (your own beauty) and blossom with joy.
23.3: Sri Raag, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make this body the field and (your) deeds the seed, and water it with (the Name of) the Lord, Saringpani.
Let the mind be the farmer, and make the Lord sprout in your heart; thus you will attain the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled.
O fool, why are you proud of Maya?
Father, son, wife, mother: none of them all will be your companions at the end.
(One who) weeds out the wicked vices of the senses, and, forsaking them, turns within and meditates (on God):
when chanting, austerity and self-restraint become the guardians (of his field), the lotus (of the heart) blossoms and honey trickles from it.
If one gathers (the Naam) on all twenty-seven days (of the lunar month), and at the day's three junctures always keeps death in mind,
and recognises the Infinite One in the ten and the eighteen (scriptures), then, says Nanak, in this way the One carries him across.
24.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 3, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make (good) conduct the soil and the Shabad the seed, and water it always with the radiance of Truth.
Become a farmer and make faith (iman) sprout; O fool, this is how heaven and hell are known.
Do not think the Lord is found by mere talk.
In pride of wealth and in the glory of beauty: in this way (you) have wasted your life.
The faults in the body are the mud and this mind the frog, which has never known the worth of the lotus.
The bumblebee, the teacher, ever speaks its language; but how can (the frog) grasp it, when it has not been given understanding?
Speaking and hearing (of sermons) are words on the wind, (while) this mind is steeped in Maya.
The Master's gracious glance is on those, and they please his heart, who have taken him as the One and meditated on him.
You keep the thirty (fasts) and make the five (prayers) your companions; (beware) lest the one called Satan cut them away.
Says Nanak, you must take the road and depart; why have you hoarded goods and wealth?
24.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He alone is the Maula, the Master, who has made the world blossom and the universe green.
Blessed is the Creator, who has bound water and earth together and keeps them so.
There is death, O Mullah, death;
so live in awe of the Creator.
Only then are you a Mullah, only then a Qazi, if you know the Name of God (Khuda).
Though you may have read a great deal, no one stays (here) once life's measure is filled.
That one alone is a Qazi who has shed self-conceit and taken the one Name as his support.
The True Creator is, and will be; he does not depart, nor will he depart.
You offer the namaz at the five times, and read the Kateb (the Semitic scriptures) and the Quran.
Says Nanak, the grave is calling, and eating and drinking are left behind.
24.3: Sri Raag, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One dog and two she-dogs are with me;
every morning they bark, always at dawn.
Falsehood is my knife, and what I take by cheating is the carrion (I live on).
I live in the guise of a hunter, O Creator.
O Lord, I have neither (followed) your counsel nor done the deeds worth doing;
I live in a deformed and fearsome form.
Your one Name carries the world across;
this is my hope, this my support.
Day and night my mouth speaks slander;
low and base, I eye the homes of others;
lust and anger, cruel and vile, dwell in my body.
I live in the guise of a hunter, O Creator.
My mind is set on snares, though my garb is a holy man's;
I am a den of fraud; I cheat the land.
very clever (I count myself), and heavy is my load (of sin).
I live in the guise of a hunter, O Creator.
I have not acknowledged the good (you) have done (me); I live on what is not mine.
What face shall I show (you), wicked thief that I am?
Lowly Nanak speaks this thought:
I live in the guise of a hunter, O Creator.
24.4: Sri Raag, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In all the beings there are is the one awareness (given by God);
no one has been made without awareness.
As their awareness is, so is their path;
the One keeps the account, (and by it) you come and go.
O soul, why do you practise cleverness?
(God) takes back and gives, and makes no delay.
The beings are yours, (O Master,) and you are (the Master) of the beings;
why, O Master, should you be angry?
Even if you, O Master, were angry,
you are theirs, and they are yours.
We are of spoiled speech, and we spoil our words;
(yet) you weigh (us) on the scales of your gracious glance.
Where there is (right) conduct, there understanding is complete;
without conduct, it falls short and ever shorter.
Nanak humbly asks: what is a giani (one who truly knows) like?
He recognises his own self, and understands that One;
by the Guru's grace he reflects (on God);
such a giani is accepted in the Lord's court.
25.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You are the river, the Knower and the Seer; I, a little fish, how can I find your end?
Wherever I look, there you are; taken out of you, I burst and die.
I know neither the fisherman nor the net;
when pain strikes, then I remember you.
You fill every place, (yet) I took you to be far away;
whatever I do is done in your presence.
You see (it all), yet I deny it;
I am neither at your work nor in your Name.
As much as you give, that much I eat;
there is no second door: to whose door would I go?
soul and body, all is in your keeping.
He himself is near, he himself far, and he himself in between.
He himself sees and hears; by his power he himself makes the world.
O Nanak, what pleases him, that command alone is accepted.
25.2: Sri Raag, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The being is only something made (by the Creator); what pride can it hold in its mind?
The giving is in the hands of the Giver.
If it pleases him he gives; (if not,) he does not give.
What can come of what the created one says?
He himself is true, and it is the true that pleases him;
but the blind one (without understanding) is raw, raw, utterly raw.
He whose trees and plants they are tends and adorns them,
and as their inborn stock is, so is the name they bear.
The inner leaning is the flower, and (by it) one receives the fruit that is written;
one sows oneself, and oneself eats (the harvest).
Raw is the wall (of the body), and raw the mason (the mind) within it;
the intellect is without salt, and the taste (of life) is flat.
O Nanak, it comes right only if (the Lord himself) sets it right;
without the Name there is no acclaim.
25.3: Sri Raag, Ghar 5, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Maya) cannot be outwitted: no trickery deceives her, and no dagger can wound her.
As the Master keeps (the being), so it lives; the heart of this greedy one wavers (before her).
How can a lamp burn without oil?
Let us live out (the teaching of) the holy books and the Puranas: (let that be the oil);
let us put the fear (of God) as the wick in this body (the lamp);
and let us bring the understanding of the True One and light it.
This is the oil, and so the lamp burns.
Make this light (within), and then the Master is met.
When the Bani (the Guru's Word) takes effect in this body,
then peace comes through the service one has done;
the whole world is a coming and going.
While in the world, let service be done:
then a seat is found in the Lord's court.
Says Nanak, (then) one walks swinging one's arms, free of care.
26.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I serve my True Guru with a single mind and a single heart, in love.
The True Guru is the place of pilgrimage where the mind's desires are fulfilled; (this is known to) the one to whom he gives the understanding.
(From him) the boon the mind longs for is received; whatever one wishes, that fruit one obtains.
Let us meditate on the Name and ask for the Name; through the Name alone one merges in Sahaj.
O my mind, taste the Lord's sweet essence, and your thirst will be quenched.
Those who have tasted it through the Guru remain merged in Sahaj.
Those who have served the True Guru have found the treasure of the Naam.
Within them the Lord's sweet essence has come to dwell, and the pride of their mind is gone.
The lotus of the heart has blossomed, and their attention is fixed in Sahaj.
Their mind, made pure, stays absorbed in the Lord, and they have won honour in the Lord's court.
Rare in the world are those who serve their True Guru,
who have killed their Haumai and their sense of mine, and kept the Lord enshrined in their hearts.
I am a sacrifice to those who have come to love the Name alone.
They alone are at peace through the four ages who have the Naam, inexhaustible and infinite.
When the Guru is met, the Naam is obtained, and attachment and thirst come to an end.
The mind stays absorbed in the Lord, and stays detached while living in the home itself.
Those who have come to relish the Lord: I give myself in sacrifice to them.
O Nanak, by (the Lord's) gracious glance is the True Name obtained, the treasure of virtues.
26.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Putting on many religious garbs and practising deceit in mind and heart, one is led astray;
such a one does not find the Lord's mansion, and dying, sinks into filth.
O mind, (stay) detached within the home itself.
Truth, self-restraint and right deeds are practised only by one in whom, through the Guru, the light has dawned.
One who has conquered the mind through the Guru's Shabad attains the highest state and liberation within the home itself.
Let us meditate on the Name of the Lord, joining the gathering of the Sat Sangat.
Even if they enjoy a hundred thousand women and rule over the nine regions (the whole earth),
without the True Guru no one finds peace; again and again they fall into the cycle of births.
Those who have worn the Lord (his Name) as a necklace round their neck, fixing their mind on the Guru's feet:
riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) follow behind them, yet they have not a sesame seed's worth of craving for them.
Whatever pleases you, God, comes about; nothing else can be done.
Your servant Nanak lives by taking the Name; O Lord, give it (to me), that (I may abide) in Sahaj and in love.
27.1: Sri Raag, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone belongs to the one whose rule it is.
When the work is done through the Guru, the True One becomes manifest in the heart.
The one within whom the True One dwells: true is the renown of that true one.
Those who have merged in the True One are not parted again; they come to dwell in their own home (within).
O my Lord, for me there is no other but the Lord.
The True Guru is pure, the form of the True God; through the Shabad comes union (with him).
One who meets (him) through the Shabad stays united, the one whom he himself unites.
In the love of another, no one meets (him); such a one comes and goes again and again.
The One is at work in all; the One alone pervades (everything).
The one to whom he himself is kind merges in the Name through the Guru.
Reading and reading, the pandits and the astrologers argue and deliberate;
their mind and intellect have gone astray, they do not understand; within them is the sickness of greed.
They wander through the eighty-four lakh forms of life, and wandering, wandering, they are ruined.
One must act out what was written from before (by past deeds); no one can erase it.
Service of the True Guru is hard: one must give one's head, giving up the self.
If they join the Shabad, then the Lord is met, and all their service is accepted.
Touching the paaras, one becomes the paaras, and one's light merges in the Light.
Those for whom it was written from before: the True Guru has come and met them.
O mind, do not keep crying out that you are hungry, hungry; do not complain.
He who created the eighty-four lakh forms of life gives each one its support.
Fearless, and merciful always, he looks after all.
O Nanak, through the Guru this is understood, and the door of liberation is found.
27.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have heard (the Name) and taken it to heart come to dwell in their own home (within).
Praising the True One through the Guru's teaching, they have found the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
Those steeped in the Shabad are pure; I give myself in sacrifice to them, ever.
Those in whose heart the Lord dwells: in that heart there is light.
O my mind, meditate on the pure Lord, Har Har.
Those on whose foreheads it was written by the Lord from the start keep, through the Guru, their attention lovingly fixed (on him).
O Sants of the Lord, look closely: he dwells near, filling every place.
Those who have recognised him through the Guru's teaching see him ever present.
Those who have virtues: in their minds he ever dwells; from those full of faults he is far.
The manmukhs are empty of virtue; without the Name they pine away and die.
Those who have heard (the Name) through the Guru's Shabad and taken it to heart have meditated on that Lord in their minds.
Steeped in devotion day and night, their mind and body become pure.
The safflower's colour is false: it fades away, and (the one attached to it) weeps in sorrow.
One within whom is the light of the Name becomes steady for ever and ever.
Having received this precious gift of human birth, (the being) does not remember the Lord's Name with loving attention.
When the foot slips (at death), one cannot stay (here), and hereafter finds no place.
That moment does not come into one's hands (again); in the end one departs regretting.
The one on whom (the Lord) casts his gracious glance is saved, keeping his attention lovingly on the Lord.
Everyone does (deeds) in imitation of others; the manmukh does not gain understanding.
Those whose heart, through the Guru, is pure: their service has been accepted.
They sing the Lord's virtues, read of the Lord daily, and singing the Lord's virtues, merge (in him).
O Nanak, the speech of those who stay lovingly attuned to the Name is ever true.
28.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have meditated on the Name single-mindedly, reflecting through the Guru's teaching:
their faces are ever radiant in that true court.
They drink the nectar for ever and ever, through love of the True Name.
O brother, through the Guru there is honour always.
Let us always meditate on the Lord, Har Har; (he) washes off the filth of Haumai and removes it.
The manmukhs do not know the Name; without the Name their honour is lost.
They have not come to relish the Shabad; they are attached to the love of another.
As worms of filth they fall into filth, and in filth they are absorbed.
Fruitful is the birth of those who walk in the True Guru's will.
They save their whole family line; blessed is the mother who bore them.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is meditated on by the one to whom (the Lord), in his will, shows grace.
Those who, through the Guru, have meditated on the Name, casting out the self from within,
are pure within and without; merging in the True One, they become true.
O Nanak, approved is the coming (into the world) of those who meditate on the Lord through the Guru's teaching.
28.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
For the Lord's devotees the wealth of the Lord is their capital; consulting the Guru, they carry on their trade.
They praise the Lord's Name for ever and ever; the Lord's Name is their merchandise and their support.
The Perfect Guru has fixed the Lord's Name firmly within them; for the Lord's devotees it is a store that never runs out.
O brother, make this mind understand:
O mind, why are you idle? Through the Guru, meditate on the Name.
Devotion to the Lord is love for the Lord, if one reflects through the Guru.
Devotion does not come through hypocrisy; double-minded speech brings only ruin.
The one within whom is discerning thought does not blend in, even when made to mix (with the false).
He alone is called the Lord's servant who keeps the Lord enshrined in his heart,
who surrenders mind and body and places them before him, killing Haumai from within.
Blessed is that Gurmukh; he is approved, who never comes back defeated.
Only if he meets (us) in his grace is he found; without his grace he cannot be found.
The eighty-four lakh forms of life long (for him); the one he unites comes and meets the Lord.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh has found the Lord, and ever stays merged in the Lord's Name.
29.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Lord's Name is an ocean of peace; it is found through the Guru.
Let us meditate on the Name day and night; (so) one merges, in Sahaj, in the Name.
The heart within is absorbed in the True Lord, and the tongue sings the Lord's virtues.
O brother, the world is in pain through the love of another.
In the Guru's refuge you will find peace, meditating on the Name day and night.
No filth clings to the True One; meditating on the Lord, the mind (too) becomes pure.
Through the Guru let us recognise the Shabad; (then) one merges in the Lord's nectar-like Name.
When the Guru's blazing wisdom is lit (within), the darkness of ignorance departs.
The manmukhs are soiled and full of filth; Haumai and craving are their sickness.
Without the Shabad the filth is not washed off; they die and are born again, ruined.
They are entangled in the fleeting play (of the world), and find neither this shore nor the far shore.
The Gurmukh is the one who keeps chanting, austerity and self-restraint: he loves the Lord's Name.
Through the Guru, let us always meditate on the Name of the one Creator.
O Nanak, let us meditate on the Name, the support of all beings.
29.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is caught in attachment; neither bairag (longing for the Lord) nor udasi (detachment from Maya) arises in him.
He does not recognise the Shabad; he is ever in sorrow, and he loses his honour in the Lord's court.
Through the Guru, Haumai is shed; dyed in the Naam, one has peace.
O my mind, day and night, hopes forever crowd within you.
Serve the True Guru: attachment is burnt away, and one stays detached while living in one's own home.
The Gurmukh does his deeds and blossoms; (within him are) longing for the Lord and bliss.
Day and night, at every hour, he worships the Lord; having slain Haumai, he is free of care.
By great good fortune he found the Sat Sangat; (there) he found the Lord, and bliss in Sahaj.
He is the true Sadhu, he alone the bairagi, who enshrines the Naam in his heart.
The dark stain (of the vices) does not touch him within at all; he sheds his self-conceit from within.
The True Guru has shown him the treasure of the Naam; he has drunk the Lord's nectar and is satisfied.
Whoever has found (the Lord) has found him in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), by perfect fortune, through bairag.
The manmukhs wander about and do not know the True Guru; the stain of Haumai clings within them.
O Nanak, those imbued with the Shabad are dyed in the Lord's Name; but without the fear (of God), what mordant is there (to fix the dye)?
29.3: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In one's own home the merchandise is found; all the wares are within.
Keep the Naam in mind each moment; through the Guru, a rare one obtains it.
The treasure of the Naam never runs out; it is gained by great good fortune.
O my mind, give up slander, Haumai and pride.
Through the Guru, ever meditate on the dear Lord, the One Creator (Ekankar).
Radiant are the faces of the Gurmukhs, who reflect on the Guru's Shabad.
Repeating again and again in their hearts the Name of the Lord (Murari), they find peace in this world and the next.
Within their own home they have found (the Lord's) mansion, by reflecting on the Shabad of the Guru.
Those who turn their faces from the True Guru bear blackened foreheads.
Day and night they earn only sorrow, and the net of Jam keeps them ever in its sight.
Not even in a dream do they see peace; great anxiety burns them through.
The One is the giver to all; he himself bestows his grace.
Nothing can be said (of it): he gives to whomever he pleases.
O Nanak, he is found through the Guru; he himself knows (all).
30.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Serve the true Master; the True One grants glory.
By the Guru's grace he comes to dwell in the mind and drives Haumai out.
This wandering mind is held still only when he himself casts his glance of grace.
O brother, through the Guru, meditate on the Lord's Name.
(Then) the treasure of the Naam dwells in the mind for ever, and one finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion.
The manmukh's mind and body are blind; he has no shelter and no resting place.
He wanders through many births, like a crow in a deserted house (that finds nothing there).
Through the Guru's teaching there is light in the heart; through the Shabad the Lord's Name is found.
Under the poison of Maya of the three qualities, (the world) is blind; attachment to Maya is pitch darkness.
The greedy serve another (than the Lord), though they read the Vedas and proclaim them aloud.
They have wasted away and died in the poison; they reach neither this shore nor the far one.
In attachment to Maya they have forgotten the world's Father, the Cherisher.
Without the Guru (the soul) is heedless; all (the world) is bound by Jamkaal (death).
O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching, cherishing the True Name (in the heart), they are saved.
30.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The three qualities are attachment to Maya; the Gurmukh attains the fourth state.
Those whom God in his grace has united (with himself): the Lord's Name has come to dwell in their minds.
Those who have merit stored in their treasury, he brings to meet the Sat Sangat.
O brother, by the Guru's teaching, abide in the True One.
Truth and truth alone is to be earned, and one is to stay joined to the true Shabad.
Those who have recognised the Naam: I am a sacrifice to them.
Giving up self-conceit, may I fall at their feet and walk as they will.
(So) one earns the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (one's) profit, and merges in the Naam in Sahaj.
Without the Guru (the Lord's) mansion is not found, nor is the Naam obtained.
Seek out and find such a True Guru, from whom that True One is found.
(Through him one) slays the demons (of lust and the rest) and dwells in peace; whatever pleases (the Lord), that comes to be.
As one has taken the True Guru to be, such is the peace one has.
There is no doubt of this at all; let any person bring love (to the Guru, and see).
O Nanak, one Light, two forms (the Lord and the Guru); through the Shabad comes the union (with them).
31.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Leaving the nectar, (the manmukhs) are lured by the poison (of Maya), and they serve others than the Lord.
They lose their own dharma and do not understand; their (life) passes day and night in sorrow.
The blind manmukhs do not remember (the Lord); they drown and die without any water.
O mind, hasten always to the Lord's refuge.
If the Guru's Shabad dwells within, then the Lord is never forgotten.
This body is a puppet of Maya, and within it the wicked Haumai has been placed.
Coming and going, birth and death (go on); the manmukh has lost his honour.
Serving the True Guru, (the Gurmukh) has found lasting peace; his light has merged in the Light (of God).
Service of the True Guru is easy and full of peace; (the servant) receives whatever fruit he wishes for.
Continence (jat), truthful living (sat), austerity and a pure body are (his) who enshrines the Lord in his mind.
He remains in bliss always, day and night; meeting the Beloved, he finds peace.
Those who are in the True Guru's refuge: I am a sacrifice to them.
At the True One's door they receive true glory, and in Sahaj they merge in the True One.
O Nanak, only by (the Lord's) glance of grace is union found in the company of the Gurmukhs.
31.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The deeds the manmukh does are like the adornments on the body of a wife her husband has forsaken.
Her Husband does not come to her bed, and day after day she is put to shame.
She does not reach her Husband's mansion, nor does she even see (his) house and door.
O brother, meditate on the Naam with a one-pointed mind.
Whoever stays joined to the company of the Sants repeats the Name of Ram and finds peace.
The Gurmukh is ever a happy wife; she keeps her Husband (the Lord) enshrined in her heart.
They speak sweetly and walk in humility; the Husband delights in them on the bed (of the heart).
Graced with honour are those happy wives whose love for the Guru knows no bounds.
By perfect fortune the True Guru is met, when one's destiny dawns.
From within, sorrow and doubt are cut away, and peace is gained.
Whoever walks in the Guru's will suffers no sorrow at all.
In the Guru's will is the nectar; a rare one obtains it in Sahaj.
Those for whom it is destined have drunk it, shedding Haumai from within.
O Nanak, meditating on the Naam through the Guru, one is united with the True One.
31.3: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When (the soul-bride) knows the Husband (Lord) as her own, she lays her body and mind before him.
The deeds that the happy wives do, those same deeds she does.
In Sahaj she comes to sweet union with the True One, and the True One gives her glory.
O brother, without the Guru there is no devotion.
Though all may yearn for it, without the Guru devotion is not received.
The soul-bride in the love of another (than the Lord) is caught in the round of the eighty-four lakh (births).
Without the Guru sleep does not come to her; her night passes in pain.
Without the Shabad the Husband (Lord) is not found; she wastes her life in vain.
Crying I, I, she roams the world, yet wealth and riches do not (go) with her (at the end).
The blind (soul-bride) does not remember the Naam; all (the world) is bound by Jamkaal.
On meeting the True Guru she has found the wealth (of the Name), cherishing the Lord's Name in her heart.
Those dyed in the Naam are pure; through the Guru they abide in Sahaj and in love.
Their mind and body are dyed in (the Lord's) love, and the tongue relishes (the Name's) sweet taste.
O Nanak, the dye the Lord applied from the beginning does not fade.
32.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
If (the Lord) shows grace through the Guru, devotion can be done; without the Guru there is no devotion.
When he unites (one) with himself and (one) understands, then that one becomes pure.
The dear Lord is true, true is (his) Bani; through the Shabad comes union (with him).
O brother, why has one empty of devotion come into the world?
He did not serve the perfect Guru, and he has wasted his life in vain.
(The Lord) himself is the Life of the world, the Giver of peace; he himself forgives (beings) and joins them to himself.
What are these helpless beings and creatures? What can anyone say or tell?
Through the Guru he himself gives glory, and he himself has (him) do (his) service.
Seeing his family, (a man) is lured into attachment; (yet) when he departs, (none of it) goes with him.
(One who) has found the treasure of virtues by serving the True Guru: his worth cannot be told.
The Lord God is (his) companion and friend; my God becomes the helper at the end.
(One) may say in one's own mind and heart (that self-conceit is gone), and have (others) say it too, but without the Guru self-conceit does not go.
The dear Lord is the Giver, who loves devotion; in his grace he makes (devotion) dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, God himself gives honour and awareness, and through the Guru he himself gives glory.
32.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Blessed is the mother who gave (him) birth, and blessed and honoured is (his) father,
(who) by serving the True Guru has found peace, and from within whom pride has gone.
The Sants stand at (the Lord's) door and serve, and they attain the treasure of virtues.
O my mind, through the Guru, meditate on that Lord.
(Then) the Guru's Shabad dwells in the mind, and mind and body become pure.
In his grace (the Lord) has come into the home (of the heart); he himself has come and met (us).
Praise him through the Guru's Shabad, and he dyes (one) in Sahaj and in love.
(So one) merges in the True One alone; one stays united and is never parted.
Whatever is to be done, (the Lord) himself is doing; nothing else can be done.
Those long separated he has united (with himself), placing them in the True Guru's care.
He himself will have (beings) do this work; nothing else can be done.
Leaving behind Haumai and the vices, mind and body are dyed in (the Lord's) love.
Day and night the Name of the fearless, formless Lord fills the heart.
O Nanak, the infinite (Lord) himself has united (them with himself) through the perfect Shabad (of the Guru).
32.3: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Govind (the Lord of the universe) is the treasure of virtues; his limit cannot be found.
He is not found by mere talk and speech; (he is found when) Haumai goes from within.
On meeting the True Guru, one stays ever steeped in (the Lord's) fear, and (the Lord) himself comes to dwell in the mind.
O brother, a rare one understands (this) through the Guru.
Performing rites without understanding, one loses the precious gift of human birth.
Those who have tasted (the Name) have known its flavour; without tasting, one strays, lost in doubt.
The True Name is the nectar; nothing (of its taste) can be told.
In the very drinking of it one is accepted (at the Lord's door), and merges in the perfect Shabad.
If he himself gives, then (it) is received; nothing else can be done.
The gift lies in the Giver's own hand; (he grants it) through the Guru's door.
As (the Lord) has made (a being), so it has become, and such are the deeds it does.
The Naam itself is continence, truthful living and self-restraint; without the Name (none) is made pure.
By perfect fortune the Naam dwells in the mind, and through the Shabad comes union (with the Lord).
O Nanak, whoever lives in Sahaj, in (the Lord's) love, gains the virtues of the Lord (within).
33.1: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One may discipline the body and practise austerities hanging upside down, yet Haumai does not leave from within.
Even if one performs rites for the soul's sake, one never obtains the Naam.
When one dies while living, through the Guru's Shabad, the Lord's Name comes and dwells in the mind.
Hear me, my mind: hasten to the True Guru's refuge.
By the Guru's grace one is set free; the poisonous ocean of the world is crossed by the Guru's Shabad.
All that is of the three qualities is Maya; the love of another (than God) is a vice.
The pandit reads (the scriptures) but is held in the bonds of attachment; in love with Maya's poison, he does not understand.
When the True Guru is met, the trikuti, the hold of the three qualities, is loosed, and in the fourth state is the door of liberation.
The path is found from the Guru, and attachment's darkness comes to an end.
When one dies through the Shabad, one is saved and finds the door of liberation.
By the Guru's grace, one stays united with the Creator, whose Name is true.
This mind is very strong; by no device does it let (one) go.
Through the love of another it brings on suffering, and it deals out heavy punishment.
O Nanak, those attached to the Naam are saved, having lost their Haumai through the Shabad.
33.2: Sri Raag, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When (God) shows grace, the Guru is found, and (the Guru) makes the Lord's Name alone take firm root (within).
No one has found (it) without the Guru; (without him) one wastes one's life in vain.
For deeds done as a manmukh, punishment is met in the Lord's court.
O mind, put an end to the love of another.
The Lord dwells within you; through the Guru's service one finds peace.
